summary:
Public Law 118-106, the "Confirmation Of Congressional Observer Access Act of 2024" (or "COCOA Act of 2024"), amends Title III of the Help America Vote Act of 2002 (HAVA) (52 U.S.C. 21081 et seq.) to codify a statutory reference to Congress's asserted constitutional authority to send observers to federal elections and to impose an affirmative access requirement on States.

Section 2(a) restructures Title III by redesignating existing sections 304 and 305 (52 U.S.C. 21084, 21085) as sections 305 and 306, and inserting a new section 304 (codified as a note to 52 U.S.C. 21083a). Subsection (a) of new section 304 sets forth a congressional finding that, under Article I, Section 5, Clause 1 and Article I, Section 4, Clause 1 of the Constitution, Congress possesses authority to observe polling and vote-processing locations regardless of legislative action, and expressly disclaims creating any new authority or procedure, characterizing the provision as a convenient statutory reference to existing authority.

Subsection (b) requires each State to provide "designated congressional election observers" full access to observe all elements of election administration in federal elections, including areas where ballots are cast, processed, scanned, tabulated, canvassed, recounted, audited, or certified, during pre- and post-election procedures. Paragraph (2) restricts observers from handling ballots or equipment, advocating for positions or candidates, reducing ballot secrecy or voter privacy, or interfering with voting or administration. A rule of construction (paragraph (3)) preserves observers' ability to question officials.

Subsection (c) authorizes State or local election officials to remove an observer upon a "reasonable basis" to believe the observer has engaged in or imminently will engage in intimidation, deceptive practices prohibited by federal law, or disruption of election processes. A removing official must, within 24 hours, notify and provide written justification to the chair and ranking minority member of the Committee on House Administration or the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration, as applicable. A rule of construction bars removal based on mere presence absent additional indicia. Upon proper removal, the relevant committee chair or ranking member may send a replacement observer for the remaining duration.

Subsection (d) defines a "designated congressional election observer" as a House or Senate employee designated in writing by the chair or ranking minority member of the named committees (or successor committees) to gather election information, including for contested-election purposes. Subsection (e) defines "State" to include the 50 States, D.C., Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, and the Northern Mariana Islands.

Section 2(b) makes a conforming amendment to HAVA section 401 (52 U.S.C. 21111), extending its enforcement mechanism to new section 304. Section 2(c) makes corresponding clerical amendments to the table of contents. The Act contains no appropriation, authorization of appropriations, sunset, or delayed effective date; it was approved October 4, 2024.
